summary: P1+P4 (Soul Food library trust & purchasing-vs-ownership) admin orders UI verified end-to-end with one critical fix. Found and fixed a CRASH (Uncaught TypeError: Illegal constructor) on /admin/orders whenever ANY order was expanded — caused by <Lock /> being used in JSX without being imported from lucide-react, so React resolved it to the global window.Lock (Web Locks API) which is not constructible. After adding `Lock` to the lucide-react import, the expansion renders cleanly. With the fix in place, all admin flows passed against SF-2026-CZ5SB (PAID): Ownership panel renders purchased-by + granted-to + entitlement-status + active/revoked links; Mark Refunded -> entitlement='revoked', override-note shows '⚠️ Manual admin override active — admin manual refunded (timestamp)', order drops out of default Active filter and reappears under All; Library /api/payments/my-purchases EXCLUDES the refunded order; /api/payments/my-orders returns status='refunded', display_status='refunded', entitlement_status='revoked', manual_override=true, purchased_by/granted_to/owned_by_me populated; Reinstate (Paid) -> entitlement back to 'granted', order returns to Active; Revoke Access keeps order Paid and flips entitlement to revoked without status change; Grant Access regenerates active links and entitlement returns to 'granted' (toast: 'Order paid. Entitlement: granted (0 links).'). Order History page renders 'Access in Library' button for completed non-gift orders. No gift orders exist in the dataset (gift_count=0) so the pink ownership-note path could only be verified by static-code review (OrderHistory.js renders ownership-note-<order_number> when is_gift/purchase_type==='gift'); the non-gift control path (no ownership-note, Access in Library button) is verified. Target order restored to PAID/granted at end of run.

critical_code_review_comments: AdminOrders.js missing-import bug caught one of the most dangerous JSX failure modes: a referenced component that silently resolves to a global Web API constructor. Recommend an ESLint rule (e.g. react/jsx-no-undef + a no-restricted-globals on `Lock,Notification,FileReader,Image,Audio,...` when used as JSX identifiers) to prevent this regression.
AdminOrders.js is 905 lines — exceeds the 700-line guideline; consider extracting the expanded order detail / ownership panel into its own component.

Default visibility filter 'Active' silently hides refunded/cancelled orders. UX-wise an inline hint (e.g. 'N refunded orders hidden — switch to All') would help admins discover the visibility filter; currently easy to miss.

rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE: /app/frontend/src/AdminOrders.js used <Lock className=... /> inside the new Ownership & Entitlement panel (line 867) but did NOT add Lock to the lucide-react import list (only Unlock was imported). With no in-scope Lock identifier, JSX/Babel transpilation produced React.createElement(Lock, …) and at runtime the bare reference resolved to the browser global window.Lock — the Web Locks API class — which throws 'Illegal constructor' when invoked as a React component. Symptom: on every expansion of ANY order the page crashed with the red CRA overlay 'Uncaught runtime errors: TypeError: Illegal constructor' and no admin status/access controls were reachable. REPRO: 1) /admin/orders 2) click chevron on any order -> red overlay. MITIGATION (applied): add `Lock,` to the lucide-react import in AdminOrders.js. POST-FIX VERIFICATION: full P1+P4 flow (refund -> library exclude -> reinstate -> revoke -> grant) completes without errors against SF-2026-CZ5SB.
